name: Kazakh Khanate
alt: Senior, Middle and Junior Juz (Great, Middle and Little Horde)

predecessors.name: Moghulistan
predecessors.text: the Chu and Talas valleys of Moghulistan, where Kerei and Janibek settled

predecessors.name: Khanate of Sibir
predecessors.text: the Dasht (Karaganda, Aqtobe, East Kazakhstan, Qostanay) that Cliopatria takes from the Sibir shape in 1482 and 1487

predecessors.name: Uzbek Khanate of Abu L Khayr
predecessors.text: the middle and lower Syr Darya round Syghanaq, held from 1475 on Cliopatria's map

successors.name: Russian Empire
successors.text: the Kazakh steppe of the Middle and Junior jüzes, Russian-ruled from 1822-1824 and finally absorbed with Kenesary's death in 1847

ledger.x: 1465: Kerei and Janibek found the Kazakh Khanate in the Chu and Talas valleys.
1468: the Kazakh tribes take the Dasht.
1469: the capital moves from Sozaq (c.
1475: the Syr Darya lands round Syghanaq.
1487: the north Kazakh steppe passes to the Kazakhs on Cliopatria's map.
1496: Burunduk and Muhammad Shaybani divide the Syr Darya.
1510: the Uzbeks cede the Syr Darya lands north of the river to Kasym.
1520: Kasym takes the Nogai capital.
1520: the capital moves from Syghanaq to Saraishyq.
1521: the Nogai steppe is Kazakh.
1521: the Kazakh Khanate reaches the Yaik.
1521: Semirechye on Cliopatria's map.
1521: Tashkent and the south of the steppe.
1521: the capital returns from Saraishyq to Syghanaq (infobox 'Syghanaq (1521-1599)'); Kasym died about 1521 and the khanate declined sharply.
1533: the struggle for Semirechye.
1565: the struggle ends with Abdurashid's reign.
1568: the Kazakhs beat the Nogais at the Emba.
1569: the Manghit nomads east of the Ural are absorbed.
1569: the Kazakhs hold the steppe east of the Ural.
1597: Tawakkul Khan invades Transoxiana.
1599: the capital moves from Sygnak to Turkestan.
1609: the Samarkand-Andijan conquests are gone on Cliopatria's map.
1611: Esim Khan takes Tashkent.
1613: Tashkent taken a second time and held.
1643: Erdeni Batur invades Semirechye.
1658: the Dzungar frontier is fixed.
1658: eastern Semirechye passes to the Dzungars.
1684: Galdan takes Sayram.
1687: Sayram is Kazakh again.
1718: eleven cells on the Irtysh (79.6-80.6E, 50.7-51.2N) pass to the Tsardom on Cliopatria's map.
1721: the northern steppe edge goes to the Russian Empire on Cliopatria's map.
1723: the Dzungars take the southern cities.
1738: the north-western edge goes to the Russian Empire on Cliopatria's map.
1745: the Dzungar hold on the south ends.
1765: Kokand takes Tashkent for a time.
1765: Abylai retakes Tashkent.
1769: 45 cells on the Irtysh and the Altai edge (82.2-84.6E, 49.5-50.8N) pass to the Russian Empire on Cliopatria's map.
1784: Tashkent becomes independent.
1791: the Aral and Ustyurt country goes to Khiva on Cliopatria's map.
1809: the Syr Darya lands round Sayram and Turkestan go to Kokand on Cliopatria's map.
1822: the Talas and Syr Darya country goes to Kokand on Cliopatria's map.
1822: 47 cells of the lower Syr Darya come back from Khiva on Cliopatria's map (61.7-65.5E, 44.7-46.2N).
1822: Russia takes over the Middle Jüz.
1824: Russia takes over the Junior Jüz.
1837: Kenesary's revolt begins.
1837: Kenesary against Russia.
1847: Kenesary is killed and the contest ends.
1847: the Junior Jüz hatching ends with the khanate; the Juz page has the Senior jüz Kazakhs incorporated into the Russian Empire in 1845-1847.
1847: the last Kazakh khan, Kenesary, falls and the khanate ends.

wars.name: Kazakh-Shaybanid wars of Burunduk and Kasym
wars.outcome: The Shaybanids hold the southern cities from about 1495-1496; Kasym defeats Shaybani's forces in 1510 and the Uzbek Khanate agrees to give up 'all former Uzbek lands north of the Syr Darya'.

wars.name: Kasym Khan's war with the Nogai Horde
wars.outcome: Kasym captures the Nogai capital Saray-Juk in 1520; the Nogai Horde is pushed toward Astrakhan and the Kazakhs hold the steppe to the Yaik.

wars.name: Kazakh-Moghul struggle for western Moghulistan
wars.outcome: Abdurashid Khan of the Yarkent Khanate fights the Kirghiz-Kazakhs of the Great Horde for western Moghulistan; it is ultimately lost and the Moghuls are largely restricted to the Tarim Basin; Oirat and Moghul forces beat Haqnazar in Jetisu in the 1560s.

wars.name: Haqnazar's war with the Nogai Horde
wars.outcome: The Kazakhs defeat the Nogais at the Emba River in 1568 and reach Astrakhan, where Russian forces repel them; the Manghit nomads east of the Ural are absorbed by 1569.

wars.name: Tawakkul Khan's invasion of Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Tawakkul captures Tashkent, Turkistan, Andijan and Samarkand but fails to take Bukhara; Tashkent and Turkestan stay Kazakh for about 200 years under a truce with the Astrakhanids.

wars.name: Esim Khan's Tashkent campaigns
wars.outcome: Esim captures Tashkent in 1611 and again in 1613 and drives the Karakalpaks out of the middle Syr Darya in 1613.

wars.name: Kazakh-Dzungar Wars
wars.outcome: The Dzungars take eastern Semirechye (border 'from the Ayagöz River to the Talas River', 1658), Sayram in 1684 and the southern cities in 1723; they hold Jetisu and Tashkent until 1745, make the jüzes recognise their overlordship in 1740-1742 and lose their…

wars.name: Abylai's war with Kokand for Tashkent
wars.outcome: Irdana Biy of Kokand takes Tashkent for a time in 1765 and Ablay Khan retakes it.

wars.name: Kenesary Kasymov's revolt
wars.outcome: Kenesary's revolt against Russian rule and Kokand ends with his death in 1847; the Kazakh Khanate ends with him.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout: nomad pasture ranges, no treaty lines.
